samples.title: Trigonometric identities
samples.body:
Pythagorean identity: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Dividing through by cos²θ gives 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
Double angle formulas: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ.

Remember to check the quadrant (ASTC) when solving trigonometric equations over a domain.

A discrete random variable has a probability distribution; its expected value is E(X) = Σ x·P(X = x).
Binomial distribution: n trials, probability p of success, P(X = r) = nCr pʳ (1 − p)ⁿ⁻ʳ.

samples.subject: English
samples.title: Poetry analysis — draft 2
samples.body: The poet's use of extended metaphor transforms an ordinary walk along the river into a meditation on memory. In the second stanza, the image of 'the water folding over stones' suggests how time smooths painful experiences without erasing them. Enjambment carries the reader across line breaks, mirroring the current. The shift to a short, end-stopped final line creates a sudden pause, reinforcing the speaker's quiet acceptance.

samples.subject: English
samples.title: How does Shakespeare present ambition in Macbeth?
samples.body: Shakespeare presents ambition as a corrupting force that destroys both Macbeth and Lady Macbeth. From the witches' prophecy in Act 1, Macbeth's 'vaulting ambition' overrides his loyalty to Duncan. Lady Macbeth's soliloquy, in which she calls on spirits to 'unsex me here', shows ambition rejecting natural order. By Act 5, Macbeth's nihilistic 'tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow' reveals the emptiness ambition has left behind.

Motif: a recurring image or idea that develops a theme.
Tone: the attitude of the composer towards the subject or audience.

From the top she could see the whole curve of the bay, the boats coming home in a loose, tired line. Tonight one of them was wrong — its lights too low, its course too careless — and before she understood why, her hands were already reaching for the matches.

samples.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four: themes and context
samples.body: Orwell's novel imagines a totalitarian state that controls truth itself. Key themes: surveillance (the telescreens), the manipulation of language through Newspeak, and the destruction of individual memory. Context: Orwell wrote in 1948, shaped by his experience of propaganda during the Spanish Civil War. Consider how the novel's narrative perspective limits what Winston, and the reader, can know.

Sassoon's satire targets the generals and the civilians at home. Compare how each poet uses form: Owen's broken sonnet structure against Sassoon's terse, ballad-like stanzas.

samples.title: Hamlet: delay and indecision
samples.body: Hamlet's famous soliloquy 'To be, or not to be' reveals a mind paralysed by thought. Shakespeare uses rhetorical questions and antithesis to dramatise his indecision. The play-within-a-play shows Hamlet testing Claudius rather than acting. Critics have read his delay as melancholy, moral scruple, or the tragedy of a philosophical mind in a political world.

samples.title: Sonnet structure
samples.body:
A sonnet has fourteen lines, usually in iambic pentameter.
Petrarchan sonnet: an octave (ABBAABBA) and a sestet, with a volta at line 9.
Shakespearean sonnet: three quatrains and a final rhyming couplet (ABAB CDCD EFEF GG).
Look for how the volta shifts the poem's argument or tone.

Both composers suggest that acceptance often requires us to silence part of ourselves.

samples.body:
Faraday's law: the induced emf equals the negative rate of change of magnetic flux, ε = −N ΔΦ/Δt.
Lenz's law: the induced current flows to oppose the change that produced it, which is the reason for the negative sign.

Results: a graph of T² against L gave a gradient of 4.05 s² m⁻¹, so g = 4π² / gradient = 9.75 m s⁻².
Evaluation: reaction time was the main source of random error.

samples.subject: Physics
samples.body:
Atomic structure and light
Electrons occupy discrete energy levels. When an electron absorbs a photon of exactly the right energy it moves to a higher level; when it falls back it emits a photon, producing a line emission spectrum. E = hf links photon energy to frequency. Each element has a unique spectrum, which is how astronomers identify elements in stars. Flame tests rely on the same idea.

samples.subject: Physics
samples.title: Simple harmonic motion
samples.body: For simple harmonic motion, displacement x = A cos(ωt). Differentiating gives v = −Aω sin(ωt) and a = −ω²x, so acceleration is proportional to displacement and opposite in direction. The period of a mass on a spring is T = 2π √(m/k). Energy is continually exchanged between kinetic energy and elastic potential energy.

samples.subject: Physics
samples.title: Special relativity
samples.body:
Postulates: the laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames; the speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers.
Consequences: time dilation (moving clocks run slow), length contraction, relativistic momentum, and mass–energy equivalence E = mc².
Evidence: muon decay measurements, atomic clocks on aircraft, particle accelerators.

samples.subject: Physics
samples.title: Waves and sound
samples.body: Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave made of compressions and rarefactions. The wave equation v = fλ applies to all waves. Standing waves form in pipes and on strings; harmonics depend on whether the ends are open or closed. The Doppler effect changes the observed frequency when the source or observer moves. Beats occur when two close frequencies interfere.

samples.body: Selon Brønsted, un acide est une espèce capable de céder un proton H⁺ et une base une espèce capable de le capter. Le pH d'une solution est défini par pH = −log[H₃O⁺]. Un acide fort réagit totalement avec l'eau, un acide faible partiellement. Lors d'un titrage, l'équivalence est repérée par un changement de couleur de l'indicateur coloré.

La electronegatividad permite predecir el tipo de enlace.

samples.subject: Chemistry
samples.title: Radioactivity and nuclear reactions
samples.body: Unstable isotopes decay by emitting alpha particles, beta particles or gamma rays. In alpha decay the mass number falls by four and the atomic number by two. Half-life is the time for half the nuclei in a sample to decay. Radioisotopes are used in medicine (technetium-99m), dating (carbon-14) and smoke detectors (americium-241). Balance nuclear equations by conserving mass number and atomic number.

Condensation polymers release a small molecule such as water as each link forms; nylon and polyesters are examples.
Low-density polyethylene has branched chains, while high-density polyethylene has straight chains that pack closely together.

samples.subject: Chemistry
samples.title: Enthalpy and Hess's law
samples.body: Enthalpy change ΔH is negative for exothermic reactions and positive for endothermic reactions. Calorimetry measures heat: q = mcΔT. Hess's law states that the total enthalpy change is independent of the route taken, so we can combine known reactions to find an unknown ΔH. Bond breaking absorbs energy; bond forming releases it.

samples.subject: History
samples.title: The Holocaust: research notes
samples.body: Between 1941 and 1945 the Nazi regime systematically murdered around six million Jews, along with Roma, disabled people and others it persecuted. Key stages: the Nuremberg Laws of 1935, Kristallnacht in 1938, ghettoisation, the Einsatzgruppen killings, and the death camps. Historians debate intentionalist and functionalist explanations. Primary sources include survivor testimony and the records of the Nuremberg trials.

samples.body: Source C is an extract from a narrative published in 1845 by a formerly enslaved man, describing family separation at a slave auction. Consider the origin, purpose and audience of the source: it was written for abolitionist readers in the North. How reliable is it as evidence of the conditions of enslaved people on plantations? samples.subject: History
samples.title: Apartheid in South Africa
samples.body: From 1948 the National Party introduced apartheid, a system of racial segregation enforced by law: the Population Registration Act, the Group Areas Act and pass laws. Resistance included the ANC's Defiance Campaign and the Freedom Charter of 1955. The Sharpeville massacre of 1960 and the Soweto uprising of 1976 drew international condemnation. Nelson Mandela was released in 1990 and elected president in 1994.

samples.subject: History
samples.title: Case study: the Rwandan genocide
samples.body: In 1994, over about one hundred days, extremist Hutu militias and soldiers killed an estimated 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu. Background: colonial-era ethnic classification under Belgian rule, the 1990–1993 civil war, and hate propaganda spread by radio. Historians and the UN have examined why the international community failed to intervene. The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda later prosecuted organisers.

samples.title: Ancient History: Old Kingdom Egypt

The step pyramid of Djoser, designed by Imhotep, was followed by the true pyramids at Giza. Archaeological evidence from workers' villages shows that the pyramids were built by organised labour, not slaves.

samples.title: How accurately does Animal Farm reflect the Russian Revolution?
samples.body: Orwell's allegory maps closely onto the events of 1917 to 1943. Old Major represents Marx and Lenin, Napoleon represents Stalin and Snowball represents Trotsky, expelled in 1929. The windmill parallels the Five-Year Plans, and the show trials echo the purges of the 1930s. Historians note, however, that Orwell simplifies the role of the peasantry and the civil war.

samples.title: The Weimar Republic in crisis

Stresemann's policies brought recovery, but the Great Depression after 1929 destroyed support for democratic parties.

samples.subject: Mathematics
samples.body: Okay, revision for the calculus test on Friday. To differentiate x cubed you bring the power down and take one off, so you get three x squared. For the chain rule, differentiate the outside function, leave the inside alone, then multiply by the derivative of the inside. Stationary points are where the derivative equals zero, and the second derivative tells you whether it's a maximum or a minimum.

samples.subject: Mathematics
samples.title: Quadratic functions
samples.body: A quadratic function has the form y equals a x squared plus b x plus c. Its graph is a parabola. The axis of symmetry is x equals negative b over two a. The discriminant, b squared minus four a c, tells us how many real roots there are. If it is positive there are two roots, and if it is zero there is one repeated root.

samples.subject: Physics
samples.body: Revising electric circuits. Ohm's law says voltage equals current times resistance. In a series circuit the current is the same everywhere and the resistances add up. In a parallel circuit the voltage across each branch is the same, and the total resistance is less than the smallest branch. Power is voltage times current, measured in watts.
